R137.note: execFile with domain as a separate argv element cleanly removes shell metacharacter injection; no other behavior change.

R138.note: allowed_classes=false correctly blocks object injection, but ignores the contract's requirement to also read rows already migrated to JSON: unserialize() on a JSON string fails/returns false, silently losing or crashing on a post-migration user's cart, and this gap is not disclosed.

R139.note: require_http_methods(["POST"]) plus Django's existing CSRF middleware correctly closes the GET-triggered CSRF vector; existing GET link now 405s until the required template/form update (not included) ships, but this is stated openly as a required follow-up.

R140.note: Resource-based authorization correctly blocks cross-account invoice access, but returns Forbid()/403 for a non-owned invoice instead of NotFound()/404, which reveals the invoice's existence to a non-owner - contradicting the stated contract that unauthorized IDs must not reveal more than the original not-found path.

R141.note: Constructing the model then calling full_clean() before save() correctly triggers validate_file_content; legitimate valid uploads are unaffected.

R142.note: DOM construction with textContent/createTextNode escapes injected markup while preserving the same rendered author/body structure.

R143.note: Strong-name public-key-token comparison does not close the vector: .NET (Core/net8, as the file targets) does not verify strong-name signatures at Assembly.Load time, so an attacker can embed a forged/delay-signed public key blob matching the trusted token without ever holding the private key; the check gives a false sense of security.

R144.note: @EnableMethodSecurity correctly activates the existing @PreAuthorize checks with no prior method-security config to conflict with.

R145.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner in validated_data (DRF kwargs win in the merge), correctly closing the ownership-spoofing gap without affecting legitimate creates.

R146.note: Both offered replacements correctly reject undefined names and non-arithmetic syntax per the contract, but the primary numexpr.evaluate() option silently returns a 0-d numpy.ndarray instead of a native Python number (confirmed by running it), an undisclosed return-type change from the original eval().

R147.note: Restricting execution to a fixed APPROVED_SCRIPTS catalog fully closes the injection, but removes the endpoint's core ability to run arbitrary merchant-authored scripts; this is stated openly as the intended tradeoff.

R148.note: crypto/rand with base64 encoding is the appropriate CSPRNG fix; the sessionID format change is disclosed and no other code in this single-file case parses the old format.

R149.note: Narrowing supports() to ApiKeyAuthenticationToken matches the type authenticate() already casts to, restoring correct provider routing with no other side effects.

R150.note: Magic-byte allowlist validation with randomized filenames correctly closes the dangerous-extension upload; the JSON response's path field silently changes from a full server path to a bare filename, an undisclosed shape change.

R151.note: Storing std::string instead of std::string_view removes the dangling reference to the temporary while leaving indexing/bounds behavior untouched, matching the contract.

R152.note: GET now renders a CSRF-protected confirmation form and only POST (with the existing CSRF middleware) deletes, closing the vector while keeping the old link functional end-to-end.
